title: Pied vs common kingfisher: two ways to fish

scenes.headline: Two kingfishers, two ways to catch a fish.
Hovers, then plunges.
scenes.body: It hangs over the water, drops lower and lower, then dives, and can swallow small fish in flight.

scenes.headline: Waits on a perch, then dives.
scenes.body: It spots a fish, dives, grabs it and flies back out. A membrane covers its eyes underwater.

scenes.headline: The pied is more than twice as heavy

scenes.label: of its body weight: what a common kingfisher eats daily

caption:
Both live along Indian rivers, but they fish in completely different ways.

Common kingfishers nest at the end of tunnels they dig in riverbanks, usually 15 to 30 cm long.

Source: Animal Diversity Web (Ceryle rudis, Alcedo atthis). Footage: pied kingfisher, Queen Elizabeth NP; common kingfisher. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Behaviour comparison shown on real video of both species side by side; a field-ID skill viewers can use on any Indian river trail.
